what: The heuristic reconstructs static CVRP routing costs by parsing grounded operator names and using metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. It identifies locations, customers, depot, propositional loc/visited facts, load, vehicles, capacity/max_vehicles, and customer demands. During evaluation it computes two estimates over the unvisited customers: (1) a minimum-spanning-tree lower bound with start and final depot edges, and (2) a capacity- and vehicle-aware greedy nearest-neighbor route cost that can choose either direct visit or visit-via-depot transitions. The returned value is the average of these two estimates, sanitized to be non-negative and finite.
why: The CVRP domain compiles routes into direct visit actions and visit-via-depot actions, so the heuristic explicitly models both staying on the current route and starting a new route. Greedy nearest-neighbor provides a realistic remaining cost estimate, while the MST bound prevents severe underestimation in early states. Averaging the two balances accuracy and robustness across different instance sizes, capacities, and vehicle limits while remaining O(n^2) per evaluation.
